image_description: A grand, ornate pipe organ situated in a church or cathedral setting. The instrument features a symmetrical facade with multiple tiers of vertical metal pipes of varying heights, creating a stepped silhouette. The central section contains the tallest pipes, flanked by shorter pipe arrays on either side. The casing is elaborately carved wood with gilded details and decorative moldings. Below the main pipe array, there appears to be a console area, though it is partially obscured by foreground elements (possibly an altar or railing) and low lighting. Two figures in white robes are visible in the lower foreground, providing scale.

The ornate carving on the upper right wing of the organ case appears slightly warped or inconsistent in perspective compared to the left side, though this could also be due to the wide-angle lens distortion typical in such photography.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific classification of the instrument as a pipe organ and distinguish it from other large architectural structures or fake instruments.
To verify the 3D spatial relationship between the multiple layers of pipes and the casing, ensuring no 'melting' or impossible depth overlaps occur in the complex geometry.
To check if individual pipes maintain distinct boundaries without merging into each other or the background, a common failure mode in AI-generated dense arrays.
To assess overall image coherence, lighting consistency, and detect subtle texture anomalies, particularly in the foreground figures and ornate details.
